units.translation: with the well-fleeced pasturings of sheep abounding.
and thriving sheep.
and the pasturage of sheep and the livelihood of Demeter.
with the bleatings of sheep.
sheep
sheep-nurturing
nurturing sheep
of sheep-nurturing Asia. Which Archilochus had said before Aeschylus, whose words Ἀσίης μηλοτρόφου [of sheep-nurturing Asia] the scholiast on Euripides Medea 713 quoted.
sheep-slaying
slaying sheep
in sheep-slaying (Bothius added ἐν [in]) delusions.
truly, indeed
in Doric μάν [truly] indeed, however
in a question τί μήν [what indeed?] what then?
combined with other particles
καὶ μὴν – γε [and indeed – at least]
ἀλλὰ μήν [but indeed] and ἀλλὰ μήν [but indeed]
οὐ μήν [not indeed] and οὐ μὴν γε [not indeed at least]
οὐδὲ μήν [nor indeed], ἀλλ᾽ οὐδὲ μήν [but nor indeed], οὔτε μήν [neither indeed]
γε μήν [at least indeed]
lead up indeed the house (thus Hermann for δόμοις [to the houses]).
go indeed, city-ruling blessed gods, rejoicing.
CHORUS: You prophesied that the stranger should kill his mother. APOLLO: I prophesied that he should exact the penalty for his father. What then?
Most common is εἶναι καὶ μὴν ἀριθμὸν ἔξοχον σοφισμάτων ἐξηθρον [to be and indeed I found out the number surpassing of wise devices].
and indeed in deed and no longer in word the earth has been shaken.

and indeed this lord himself is the offspring of Oedipus. Thus καὶ μήν [and indeed] more often in Sophocles when the arrival of a new person is to be indicated: about which I have spoken in the Lexicon Sophocleum p. 242a and 302a.
and indeed I will tell the one who obtained from there the lot at the gates.
and indeed from us the sound of the Persian tongue came to meet.
and indeed say this not against my judgment.
and indeed the oracle will no longer be seeing from under veils.
and indeed I know the Greek speech too well.
and indeed this one is very much like-winged to see.
and indeed – an honor for the tomb of the unlamented fortune.
and indeed I am an adviser not at all to dishonor this grievous company of the land.
and indeed he came to Canobus and to Memphis.
and indeed of these old mockeries for you.
and indeed you do not yet know how to be wise.
and indeed I would repay him thanks as owing.
and indeed I hear the neighings of horses.
and indeed being present at least.
and indeed we long for another at least.
and indeed having drunk at least.
and indeed the tracks of feet are similar.
(in Bekker's Anecdota p. 321, 19) and indeed I love at least and these things are not loathsome to me. Thus Bekker for φιλῶ γὰρ ἀβδέλυκτ᾽ ἐμοί [for I love, not loathsome to me].
but indeed well-disposed at least is the first judge of these dreams.
but indeed my son desired to hunt this city.
but I indeed with oar at the ready do not refuse to die, where the unusual placement of the particle is to be noted, unless ἀλλὰ μὴν κἀγώ [but indeed I too] should be written with Porson.
not indeed by such penalties at least did I think I would be wasted away.
not indeed without boasting at least does he stand at the gates.
not indeed having thrown away more will I be dishonored.
not indeed unhonored at least by the gods will we die.
nor indeed without dispute having been overwhelmed.
but nor indeed did she who killed him shear him.
nor indeed is it lawful for me.
nor indeed in the misery of the paternal land.
from this seed indeed at least a bold one will be born.
you indeed at least will obtain many mourners.
with time indeed at least.
wingless indeed at least to see these.
